text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"algorithmic_rent_setting","status":"not_yet_effective","title":"Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act","requirement":"Makes it unlawful, and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, for a rental property owner (or its agent, representative or subcontractor) to pay for or subscribe to the services of a coordinator. It is also unlawful for a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition, including by performing a coordinating function. Two or more persons may not engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. Agents or representatives of a coordinator may not engage in parallel pricing coordination. No person may perform a coordinating function. A coordinating function includes collecting competitively sensitive information of two or more owners to train or run an algorithm that sets or recommends rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. It also includes setting rents, lease terms or occupancy levels with an algorithm that uses other owners' competitively sensitive information. Finally, it includes recommending the same or a substantially similar algorithmic output to two or more owners in a way that facilitates parallel pricing coordination. Exclusions: research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices; and government entities setting rents through affordability controls. The Attorney General must set up a complaint location and may adopt rules.
